## Overview

::: {.summary}

📘 **HTML**
HyperText Markup Language is the **standard markup language for creating web pages**. It describes the **structure** of a page as a tree of **elements**: "this is a heading", "this is a paragraph", "this is a link", and so on.

React does not replace HTML: every React component ends up **rendering HTML elements into the DOM**. JSX is just HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript, so **knowing HTML well is the first step to writing good JSX**.

:::

---

## Why HTML before React?

When we write a component like this:

``` {.jsx .code-overflow-wrap filename="Hello.jsx"}
export default function Hello() {
  return <h1 className="title">Hello, students!</h1>;
}
```

the browser never sees JSX. React translates it and finally the DOM contains a plain `<h1 class="title">`. So:

- the **tags** we use in JSX are HTML tags (`div`, `p`, `ul`, `form`, `button`...),
- the **attributes** are (almost) HTML attributes (`src`, `alt`, `href`, `type`...),
- the **events** we handle in React (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`) are the browser's HTML DOM events (see [Events and the DOM](/reactjs/reactjs-what-html-events.qmd)).

::: {.callout-tip}
## HTML is the output of React
If you know which HTML you want in the browser, writing the JSX is easy. If you don't, React only makes it harder.
:::

## HTML document structure

A minimal HTML5 document looks like this:

``` {.html .code-overflow-wrap filename="index.html"}
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>My first page</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  </head>
  <body>
    <h1>My first heading</h1>
    <p>My first paragraph.</p>

    <script src="app.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

- `<!DOCTYPE html>` tells the browser this is an **HTML5** document.
- `<html>` is the **root element** of the page.
- `<head>` holds **meta information**, not shown on the page:
  - `<meta charset>`: character encoding (use `UTF-8`).
  - `<meta name="viewport">`: makes the page responsive on mobile.
  - `<title>`: the text in the browser tab (and in search results).
  - `<link>`: links external resources, mostly CSS stylesheets.
  - `<script>`: JavaScript, inline or from a file (`src`). It can also go at the end of `<body>`.
- `<body>` contains **everything visible**: headings, paragraphs, images, links, tables, lists...

### Elements, tags and empty elements

An **element** is a start tag, some content and an end tag:

``` html
<p>This is a paragraph.</p>
<!-- start tag ^      ^ end tag -->
```

Elements can be **nested** (an element inside another element), and that nesting is what builds the **DOM tree**.

Some elements have **no content** and no end tag: they are **empty elements**, like `<br>`, `<img>`, `<input>`, `<meta>` or `<link>`.

::: {.callout-important}
## In JSX every tag must be closed
HTML accepts `<br>` and `<img src="a.png">`, but JSX does not. In React you must write `<br />` and `<img src="a.png" />`.
:::

## The most relevant tags

### Text

``` html
<h1>Main title</h1>          <!-- h1 ... h6: headings, h1 is the most important -->
<h2>Section title</h2>
<p>A paragraph with <strong>important</strong> and <em>emphasised</em> text.<br>
   And a line break.</p>
<hr>                          <!-- a thematic break (horizontal line) -->
```

- Use **one `<h1>` per page** and keep headings in order (`h1` → `h2` → `h3`): search engines and screen readers use them to understand the page.
- `<strong>` and `<em>` add **meaning** (importance, emphasis), not only bold or italic style.
- Browsers ignore extra spaces and line breaks in the source: use `<p>` and `<br>`.

### Links and images

``` html
<a href="https://www.w3schools.com/html/" target="_blank">W3Schools HTML tutorial</a>
<a href="/reactjs/reactjs-what-jsx.html">Relative link to another page</a>

<img src="images/react-logo.png" alt="React logo" width="200">
```

- `<a>` (anchor) creates a **hyperlink**; `href` is the destination and `target="_blank"` opens it in a new tab.
- `<img>` is empty; `src` is the path to the image and `alt` is the **alternative text**, shown if the image fails and read by screen readers. Always write an `alt`.

### Lists

``` html
<ul>                <!-- unordered list (bullets) -->
  <li>HTML</li>
  <li>CSS</li>
</ul>

<ol>                <!-- ordered list (numbers) -->
  <li>Learn HTML</li>
  <li>Learn React</li>
</ol>
```

Lists are everywhere in React: a todo list, a menu, a list of products. Later you will render them with `array.map()`.

### Tables

``` html
<table>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Name</th><th>Role</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Ada</td><td>Frontend</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Linus</td><td>Backend</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

- `<tr>` is a table row, `<th>` a header cell and `<td>` a data cell.
- `<thead>` and `<tbody>` group the header rows and the body rows.

### Containers: `div` and `span`

``` html
<div class="card">
  <h3>Card title</h3>
  <p>Some text with a <span class="highlight">highlighted</span> word.</p>
</div>
```

- `<div>` is a **block-level** element: it always starts on a new line and takes the full width.
- `<span>` is an **inline** element: it only takes the width it needs and stays inside the text.
- Neither has any meaning: they are generic boxes to group content and style it with CSS.

### Semantic elements (layout)

**Semantic** elements are elements **with meaning**: the name tells the browser and the developer what the content is. Instead of `<div id="nav">` or `<div class="footer">`, HTML5 gives us:

``` {.html .code-overflow-wrap filename="layout.html"}
<body>
  <header>
    <h1>My shop</h1>
    <nav>
      <a href="/">Home</a> | <a href="/products">Products</a>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>
    <section>
      <h2>New products</h2>
      <article>
        <h3>Keyboard</h3>
        <p>Mechanical keyboard, 45 €.</p>
      </article>
    </section>
    <aside>Offers of the week</aside>
  </main>

  <footer>© 2026 My shop</footer>
</body>
```

| Element     | Meaning                                                    |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `<header>`  | Introductory content: logo, title, navigation              |
| `<nav>`     | A block of navigation links                                |
| `<main>`    | The main content of the page (only one per page)           |
| `<section>` | A thematic group of content, usually with a heading        |
| `<article>` | Independent, self-contained content (a post, a product)    |
| `<aside>`   | Content aside from the main content (a sidebar)            |
| `<footer>`  | Footer of the page or of a section: author, copyright, links |

::: {.column-margin}
In React, a page layout is usually split into components with the same names: `<Header />`, `<Nav />`, `<Main />`, `<Footer />`. Each component returns its semantic HTML element.
:::

## Attributes

Attributes give **extra information** about an element. They always go in the **start tag** as `name="value"`.

| Attribute | Used on               | What it does                                              |
|-----------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `id`      | any element           | A **unique** identifier in the page (for CSS, JS, labels) |
| `class`   | any element           | One or more class names, shared by many elements (CSS)    |
| `style`   | any element           | Inline CSS: `style="color:red; font-size:20px"`           |
| `href`    | `<a>`, `<link>`       | URL of the link or resource                               |
| `src`     | `<img>`, `<script>`   | Path of the image or script                               |
| `alt`     | `<img>`               | Alternative text for the image                            |
| `type`    | `<input>`, `<button>` | Kind of input or button                                   |
| `name`    | form fields           | Key of the field when the form is sent                    |
| `value`   | form fields           | Current or initial value of the field                     |
| `lang`    | `<html>`              | Language of the page                                      |

: Most common HTML attributes {.striped .hover}

## Summary

| Group       | Tags                                                                 |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Structure   | `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, `<body>`, `<meta>`, `<title>`, `<link>`, `<script>` |
| Text        | `<h1>`–`<h6>`, `<p>`, `<strong>`, `<em>`, `<br>`, `<hr>`             |
| Links/media | `<a>`, `<img>`                                                       |
| Lists       | `<ul>`, `<ol>`, `<li>`                                               |
| Tables      | `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, `<td>`              |
| Containers  | `<div>` (block), `<span>` (inline)                                   |
| Semantic    | `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>` |

: HTML tags cheat sheet {.striped .hover}

Forms have their own article: [HTML forms](/reactjs/reactjs-what-html-forms.qmd).
